sections.content: To say 'my X,' add a possessive suffix to the noun. Vowel-final nouns usually just take -m, often lengthening the last vowel: anya → anyám, apa → apám. Consonant-final nouns need a linking vowel that follows harmony: család → családom.
sections.title: Saying 'my'

sections.content: Watch the vowel change: anya becomes anyám and apa becomes apám (a → á) — this lengthening is common in possessives and just has to be learned word by word.
